title: Cost-of-living riots in Milan, Turin and Bologna
deck: Two nights of rioting around Milan's Duomo turned into a month of strikes and marches over prices, wages and jobs, and they now shape the run-up to Italy's 2027 election.

fuel.title: Thousands march against high prices
fuel.how: Street anger over prices and the cost of living is the common thread that keeps the October riots from fading.

fuel.title: Second nationwide general strike in two weeks
fuel.how: Unions and workers joined the unrest with a general strike that paralysed transport and put pressure on the government.

fuel.title: Separate protest movements merge into one
fuel.how: Mass marches on 31 October brought disparate movements together, widening the crowds and the list of grievances.

fuel.title: Italian bond spreads widen with France's
fuel.how: Italian spreads moved in step with French ones in early October, raising Rome's borrowing costs and leaving less money to ease price anger.

fuel.title: Iran war keeps pump prices high
fuel.how: Strikes on Iran since 28 February 2026 have kept oil and freight costs elevated, and fuel is the most visible price Italians cite.

card.headline: Italy's riots began as price anger in Milan and have grown into a national protest and strike movement

keyNumber.label: arrests in Milan over 17-18 October, with clashes also in Turin and Bologna

forYou.line: Italy has now had two general strikes in about two weeks, and transport was paralysed on the latest. Expect disruption on any announced strike day.
Looting around Milan's Duomo hit the city's most visited area. Expect more security and some lost trade near protest routes.
Italian bond spreads widened in step with France's in early October. Italy is exposed to any further French stress.
The deeper issue is politics: Meloni is positioning on order ahead of a 2027 election, while the protests are about prices and wages.

effects.text: Rioting and looting around Milan's Duomo, with clashes in Turin and Bologna; more than 200 arrests over 17-18 October
Thousands march across Italy against high prices and the rising cost of living
A nationwide general strike, Italy's second in about two weeks, paralyses transport
Separate protest movements unite in mass marches on 31 October
Italian bond spreads widened with France's in early October, raising Rome's borrowing costs
Prime Minister Meloni calls a security meeting and frames the government around order
Less fiscal room to ease prices if interest costs rise; fuel stays dear while the Iran war keeps oil high
University occupations, such as the Einaudi Campus in Turin, continue into November
Further strikes and marches are likely to disrupt transport and trade in city centres
The 2027 election campaign is likely to turn on order versus living costs
Unrest across Europe (France, Germany, Switzerland) raises the chance of copycat flare-ups
If French stress deepens, investors may price more political risk into Italian debt
A right-wing Europe split on Ukraine could widen if Meloni and Le Pen head into elections on opposite lines

whatHappened: On 17 and 18 October 2026, rioting and looting broke out around Milan's Duomo. More than 200 people were arrested over the two days, according to Euronews. There were also clashes in Turin and Bologna. The demonstrations were against the cost of living.

The unrest did not stop there. On 31 October, Le Monde reported mass demonstrations across Italy that brought disparate protest movements together. On about 1 November, a general strike, the second in roughly two weeks, paralysed transport. Reuters reported mass protests across the country.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called a security meeting after the riots. Italy holds a parliamentary election in 2027. Elsewhere in Europe, French unrest and scattered riots in Germany and Switzerland happened around the same time. The headlines we have do not give crowd counts for Italy's marches.
whyItMatters: Living costs come first. The marches are about prices, rents and wages. Italy's anger resembles France's, because both are squeezed households, though neither caused the other. Easing the squeeze would calm both.

Jobs and wages give the anger organisation. A general strike moves the story from night-time rioting to a mass movement with union backing. A second strike within about two weeks suggests the pressure is not fading quickly.

Politics decides what the anger turns into. Separate movements merged on 31 October. Disorder before a vote tends to favour whoever promises order, and Meloni is already positioning that way. The same wave is a test of whether Europe's right stays united on Russia, since Meloni backs continued Ukraine support and Le Pen does not.

Markets limit the government's room to respond. Italian spreads widened in step with France's in early October. Paying more interest leaves Rome less to spend on soothing price anger. France faces a Moody's review and a record borrowing need in 2027, so French stress can pass quickly to Italy.

Energy keeps the pressure on. Strikes on Iran that began on 28 February 2026 have kept oil and freight costs high for eight months. Fuel is the most visible price Italians see every time they fill up, and the demonstrations cite it.

winners.why: Disorder before an election usually helps those promising law and order. Meloni's government is positioning on exactly that.
Demand for protection and riot cover tends to rise after looting in prime shopping districts.
Two general strikes and the merging of protest movements show strong mobilising power.

losers.why: Looting hit the Duomo area, and strike and protest days reduce footfall.
Transport was paralysed on the latest general strike.
The core grievance is high prices, and fuel stays costly while the Iran war lasts.
It must defend order, fund relief and keep bond markets calm at the same time, a hard mix when borrowing costs are rising.

whatsNext: Early November: the Turin campus occupation continues, and the university has reopened distance learning.
November to December: the government's budget goes through parliament. Pressure from strikes and bond markets will shape it.
Watch for a third general strike, further clashes in Milan, Turin or Bologna, and any copycat unrest in neighbouring countries.
2027: Italy's parliamentary election. Order versus living costs is the likely battleground.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: what is the most likely path for Italy's protests over the next few months?
options: Rapid calm as the government offers relief
Simmering unrest with periodic strikes and flare-ups
Escalation into a sustained national crisis
A bond-market shock forces an emergency budget
predict.explanation: Our base case, at about 45%, is simmering unrest. Strikes and marches continue at intervals, violence stays local, and the government leans on order messaging. Escalation is second at about 25%.

recap.question: Where did the October rioting begin?
What did the general strike around 1 November do?
What kind of politics does disorder before a vote tend to favour?

timeline.title: Strikes on Iran begin
timeline.detail: The oil and freight shock that follows keeps fuel prices elevated for eight months and feeds the price anger behind later protests.

timeline.title: Italian spreads widen with France's (approximate, early October)
timeline.detail: French borrowing costs reach their widest premium over Germany since the euro-debt crisis, and Italy's rise with them. Rome's interest bill and room to spend are squeezed.

timeline.title: Rioting and looting begin around Milan's Duomo
timeline.detail: Cost-of-living demonstrations turn violent in the city's centre. The same day, hundreds of thousands march in France over similar grievances.

timeline.title: Second day of clashes
timeline.detail: Fighting continues in Milan, with clashes also in Turin and Bologna. More than 200 people are arrested over the two days. Euronews's headline ties the figure to the second day.

timeline.title: Meloni calls a security meeting
timeline.detail: The government frames its response around order as Euronews reports the arrests. Italy's election is due in 2027.

timeline.title: Mass demonstrations unite protest movements
timeline.detail: Le Monde reports that marches across Italy brought disparate movements together, widening the crowds and grievances.

timeline.title: Second general strike in about two weeks
timeline.detail: Transport is paralysed and mass protests sweep Italy. Separately, thousands march against high prices.

timeline.title: Telegraph reports Meloni targeting the wealthy with an 'exit tax'
timeline.detail: The headline suggests the government is trying to answer fairness complaints. We do not have details of the measure.

timeline.title: Turin campus occupation continues; school staff cuts reported
timeline.detail: The Einaudi Campus occupation goes on while the university reopens distance learning. Reuters reports Italy is cutting school staff as the demographic crisis bites.

causes.name: Squeezed household budgets
causes.detail: Prices, rents and wages are straining households in Italy as in France. Housing and wages are central grievances.

causes.name: Limited fiscal room
causes.detail: With borrowing costs sensitive to French and eurozone stress, Rome has less money to ease price pressure.

causes.name: Demographic and public-service strain
causes.detail: Reuters reports Italy cutting school staff as population decline bites, a source of friction in education.

causes.name: Cost-of-living demonstration
causes.detail: A demonstration against prices and the cost of living turned into rioting and looting around the Duomo.

causes.name: Spillover from France
causes.detail: The same weekend saw large French marches over the same grievances. Neither caused the other.

causes.name: Fuel prices
causes.detail: The Iran war keeps oil and pump prices high, the most visible rising price.

causes.name: Union mobilisation
causes.detail: A second general strike in about two weeks gave the movement organisation and reach.

causes.name: Merging movements
causes.detail: Separate protest movements joined forces on 31 October.

causes.name: Student occupations
causes.detail: University occupations, such as in Turin, added a youth strand, mirroring wider European youth unrest.

stakeholders.name: Giorgia Meloni
stakeholders.wants: Restore order and keep her coalition's lead into the 2027 election
stakeholders.leverage: Police and security powers, the budget, the agenda
stakeholders.likelyMove: Stress security, offer targeted relief and fairness measures such as the reported exit tax, avoid broad spending

stakeholders.name: Matteo Salvini
stakeholders.wants: Frame the unrest as a threat from the left and from political Islam, as a headline from 31 October quotes him
stakeholders.leverage: A party in government and a clear law-and-order message
stakeholders.likelyMove: Harder line on protesters and migration, which could pull the coalition's tone to the right

stakeholders.name: Trade unions
stakeholders.wants: Wage and price relief, concessions in the budget
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep calling strikes while the budget is debated

stakeholders.name: Student and campus occupiers
stakeholders.role: Youth strand of the movement, such as at Turin's Einaudi Campus
stakeholders.wants: Better funding, no school staff cuts, lower living costs
stakeholders.leverage: Occupations and the ability to join wider marches

stakeholders.name: Opposition parties
stakeholders.wants: Turn price anger into votes without being tied to the rioting
stakeholders.leverage: Parliamentary budget debate and street links
stakeholders.likelyMove: Condemn violence while backing the cost-of-living grievances

stakeholders.name: Bond investors and the ECB
stakeholders.wants: A credible fiscal path and no fresh French shock
stakeholders.likelyMove: Watch the French budget and the Moody's review; the ECB has said intervention is not warranted

sectors.sector: Retail and tourism in Milan's centre
sectors.why: Looting hit the Duomo area, and marches and strikes cut footfall on protest days.
The general strike paralysed transport, and more strike days are possible.
Spreads widened with France's in early October. Italian banks hold large amounts of Italian debt, so wider spreads weigh on them. This is an inference.
Demand for protection and riot cover tends to rise after looting.
Occupations disrupt teaching, and staff cuts add to the strain. Remote learning limits the immediate damage.
Pump prices stay high while the Iran war keeps oil elevated, squeezing households and transport firms.
A reported 'exit tax' on the wealthy could change behaviour. We have no details, so this is speculative.

dailyLife.effect: Oil and freight costs have been elevated for eight months, and fuel is the most visible rising price for Italians.
Two general strikes in about two weeks have paralysed transport. Check strike calendars before travel.
Marches and occasional clashes can close streets and shops in Milan, Turin and Bologna.
The Einaudi Campus in Turin is still occupied, and the university has reopened distance learning.
Reuters reports Italy is cutting school staff because of demographic decline, which may add to local friction.
If Italian spreads stay wide, borrowing costs for the state and, over time, households can rise. This is an inference.

scenarios.name: Simmering unrest
scenarios.looksLike: Strikes and marches continue at intervals, flare-ups stay local, the government leans on order messaging and targeted relief, and the budget passes with small changes.
signposts: Turnout on strike days stays steady or falls
No serious injury or death in the streets
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Italy stays distracted and cautious, and Meloni enters 2027 with an order-versus-prices fight.

scenarios.name: Rolling escalation
scenarios.looksLike: More general strikes, repeated rioting in several cities, protest restrictions, and a hardening of both sides.
signposts: A death or serious injury in clashes
A third general strike within a month
Unrest in Germany, Switzerland or France intensifying in step
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Copycat unrest spreads across Europe, and the 2027 campaigns turn more polarised.

scenarios.name: Relief and de-escalation
scenarios.looksLike: The government offers visible price or wage relief, unions accept talks, and the movements split.
signposts: Budget measures aimed at wages or energy bills
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Calmer streets, a wider deficit, and modest market pressure.

scenarios.name: Market shock
scenarios.looksLike: French stress deepens, Italian spreads spike, Rome must tighten its budget, and anger rises as money for relief shrinks.
signposts: Italian spreads widening sharply and moving with French ones
scenarios.effectOnWorld: A eurozone-wide stress test, with fights over ECB support and weaker backing for Ukraine.

predictions.text: Italy will see at least one more nationwide strike or mass march over prices and wages before 31 January 2027. Probability about 70%.
Serious rioting on the scale of 17-18 October (100+ arrests in a single city over a weekend) will recur in an Italian city. Probability about 25%.
The Italian budget will pass in 2026 without a major government crisis. Probability about 85%.
The Italian-German 10-year spread will stay below 200 basis points through year-end. This is an estimate with limited data in our sources. Probability about 85%.
Law and order will rank alongside living costs as a leading theme in Italian election polling and coverage in the first half of 2027. Probability about 65%.

actions: Build buffer time into lanes through Italian cities and transport hubs on announced strike days.
Review security and insurance cover for stores and sites in Milan, Turin and Bologna.
Brief staff on protest routes and give flexible work options on strike days.
Add fuel-surcharge and force-majeure clauses to contracts touching Italy.
Watch the Italian-German spread and French headlines together, since they moved in step in early October.
Treat Italian political risk as tied to both the budget and the 2027 election.
Do not assume an ECB backstop; officials have said conditions for intervention are not met.
Check strike calendars before travel and childcare plans.
Expect fuel and food prices to stay elevated while the Iran war continues.
Where borrowing is needed, consider fixed-rate options while rates are volatile.
Separate order from grievances: prosecute violence, address the price and wage complaints behind it.
Target relief at the households most exposed to fuel and housing costs rather than broad spending.
Coordinate with France and other EU capitals on shared cost-of-living drivers and market stress.

analogues.whatFollowed: A fuel-tax rise sparked weekly protests that forced concessions and a larger deficit. The movement faded, but the grievances did not.
Street protests gave way to election-season politics. Anti-establishment parties kept gaining ground. Details are from general knowledge and the match is loose.
Large demonstrations over energy bills pushed governments into relief packages. Many governments faced election pressure afterwards. Based on general knowledge.

watch.title: Italian budget law deadline (approximate)
watch.why: The budget is the main vehicle for price and wage relief, and the test of Rome's fiscal room.

watch.title: A third general strike
watch.why: Two strikes in about two weeks show momentum. A third would signal a sustained campaign.

watch.title: Turin's Einaudi Campus occupation
watch.why: Whether it ends, spreads to other campuses or draws police action will show how the youth strand develops.

watch.title: Italian-German spread and French headlines
watch.why: Spreads moved in step with France's in early October. A French shock would cut Rome's room to manoeuvre.

watch.title: Pump prices and the Iran war
watch.why: Fuel is the most visible price. A spike would likely reignite protests faster than any budget measure.

watch.title: Meloni's security measures and the 'exit tax'
watch.why: They show how the government mixes order with fairness messages ahead of 2027. Details of the tax are not in our material.

watch.title: Unrest elsewhere in Europe
watch.why: French marches and riots or arson in Germany and Switzerland suggest a shared pattern. Copycat flare-ups could return to Italy.

confidence.claim: More than 200 arrests over 17-18 October in Milan; clashes in Turin and Bologna
confidence.note: Rests mainly on one Euronews report. Its headline ties the figure to the second day, while the event summary says over both days.

confidence.claim: A second general strike in about two weeks paralysed transport around 1 November
confidence.note: Based on headlines from Latin Times, Reuters and italien.news; we did not read the full texts and have no turnout figures.

confidence.claim: Separate protest movements united in mass demonstrations on 31 October
confidence.note: Based on the Le Monde headline only.

confidence.claim: Italian spreads widened in step with France's in early October
confidence.note: Taken from the event's connection notes, not from a source we can cite with a URL here.

confidence.claim: Fuel is the most visible price and the Iran war keeps oil high
confidence.note: From connection notes; the war began on 28 February 2026. Not independently sourced here.

confidence.claim: Meloni's 'exit tax' and school staff cuts
confidence.note: Headlines only; we do not know the content or scale.
Author judgement, not sourced forecasts; to be graded as events resolve.

evidence.method: Drafted from the listed sources and 22 matched wire headlines dated up to 2 November 2026. For most items beyond the Euronews report on 19 October we had only headlines and short summaries, not full texts. Facts on bond spreads and the Iran war come from the event's connection notes. Crowd sizes, strike turnout and the details of the exit tax were not available and are not estimated. Scenario probabilities and predictions are the author's judgement. Where evidence is thin, the text is hedged.
